selection: For each NOAA PORTS station, use metadata real_time_bin as the representative current bin. Local window is 00:00-10:00 America/Chicago; displacement integrates from first available local-midnight sample.

modern_upper_bay_summary.interpretation: All 15 modern upper-bay station-event pairs had positive eastward displacement over the first 6 hours; 14/15 were eastward over 3 hours. Across the three stations, every one of the five event mornings had positive mean eastward displacement at 1, 3, and 6 hours. This is a candidate Stage-2 directional pattern, not a predictive result because the panel contains confirmed events only and no clean non-event controls.

historic_2010_point_clear_bay_mouth.name: Mobile Bay Buoy M
historic_2010_point_clear_bay_mouth.interpretation: The historic bay-mouth representative bin was strongly westward during the 2010-08-12 Point Clear event morning. This falsifies any universal requirement that the bay-mouth current itself be eastward on every Jubilee morning and reinforces the need for location/vertical-state-specific transport features.

guardrails: Upper-bay PORTS stations are not Point Clear shoreline-current observations.
The current real_time_bin is used as a stable representative vertical bin; this does not establish the same vertical layer was most relevant historically.
Event mornings only cannot estimate discrimination, false-alert rate, calibration, or causal effect.

The 00-06 local integration is largely pre-dawn for these events but may overlap event onset when exact onset is not known; do not treat it as a leakage-safe forecast feature until event-specific issue times are established.
No uncertain day is labeled a negative and no production change is authorized.
